A Typhoon Watch, Flash Flood Watch, and Coastal Flood Watch are now 
in effect for the Marianas. Fairly quiet conditions are expected to 
continue through Saturday morning, but expect to start seeing swaths 
of upper-level cirrus streaming over the islands, ahead of Typhoon 
Bavi. Showers will begin to increase Saturday evening as the far 
outer rain bands of Bavi begin to move overhead, then, northerly 
winds will begin to increase Saturday overnight. Regardless of where 
Typhoon Bavi eventually makes passage through the Marianas, 
conditions will begin to rapidly degrade for all islands Sunday, as 
tropical storm conditions begin to be felt. The timeframe and exact 
point of passage remain uncertain and will see adjustment in the 
forecast over the next 36 to 48 hours, but there is higher confidence
in Bavi arriving as a strong typhoon, potentially a Category 5 Super
Typhoon with sustained winds potentially reaching 160 mph near the 
center. See the Tropical Systems section for more details.
 

Marine...
Combined seas of 3 to 5 feet and light to moderate trade winds are 
expected through tonight for the Marianas. Seas are expected to begin
increasing by several feet Saturday ahead of Typhoon Bavi, with
combined sea heights beginning to exceed hazardous levels of 10 feet
Saturday night. Sea conditions then rapidly degrade through Sunday as
tropical storm force conditions begin to be felt over coastal waters. 
Seas of 25 to 35 feet are anticipated during the passage of Bavi late 
Sunday through Monday with seas potentially approaching 40 feet near
the center of Bavi.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon Bavi (09W), is currently located over the open ocean roughly
590 miles east of Guam, at 12.9N 153.8E. Bavi is at Category 3
strength with maximum sustained winds at 120 mph, and it continues to
strengthen. Bavi has been moving westward at around 11 knots, and the
latest forecast from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC)
maintains this general track and speed through Saturday before making
a west-northwest turn early Sunday, when it is forecast to become a
Category 5 super typhoon. Typhoon Bavi is then expected to continue
this west-northwest track across the Marianas through Monday, passing
through the islands still at potentially Category 5 strength. The
latest forecast tracks continue to show a general passage between
Rota and Tinian, but the track could shift northward or southward,
and it remains uncertain which islands will see the greatest impacts.
All islands across the Marianas will see impacts given the large 
wind field of this storm, ranging from damaging tropical storm force
winds to catastrophic super typhoon winds near the center. 
Widespread heavy rain will be likely with storm passage, capable of 
producing flooding and mudslides. The latest JTWC forecast has the 
onset of tropical storm force winds around late Sunday afternoon or 
evening, roughly 48 hours away.

For more information on Typhoon Bavi, please refer to the Tropical 
Cyclone Public Advisory issued by the National Weather Service under 
WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM and the Tropical Cyclone Warning issued by the
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
Typhoon Bavi (09W) continues to intensify roughly 500 miles northwest 
of Pohnpei. Scatterometry from this morning shows a broad area of 
moderate to fresh west to southwest winds extending across Pohnpei 
and Kosrae, which are expected to continue for Pohnpei through 
tonight as Bavi continues to move westward. Winds diminish through
the weekend as a col area moves in behind Bavi. Satellite shows
sporadic convection trailing behind TY Bavi, including to the west 
and south of Majuro, and scattered showers within the southwest 
monsoon flow over Pohnpei. The trailing convergence behind Bavi will
continue to produce at least scattered showers for Pohnpei and Kosrae 
through much of the coming week, becoming numerous at times this 
weekend closer to Pohnpei. Conditions remain fairly quiet near Majuro
and Kosrae this evening, but a weak NET disturbance and associated
convergence looks to focus scattered showers across the area
throughout much of the forecast period. 

Latest altimetry shows combined seas of roughly 3 to 5 feet near
Pohnpei and Kosrae and 4 to 6 feet near Majuro, with a south to
southeast swell expected to persist for Majuro and Kosrae behind 
Bavi for the next day or so. For Pohnpei, west to southwest swell
will move in this weekend, becoming west to northwest early next
week, emanating from TY Bavi. Overall, benign marine conditions are
expected to persist, but increasing westerly swell next week
could produce some elevated west-facing surf.
